stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: A Lebenslauf, Anschreiben, and Zeugnisse

A portfolio of creative work only

questions.topic: Direction of a German Lebenslauf
questions.learningObjective: State the direction of a German Lebenslauf

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: Chronological from oldest to newest
options.misconception: treats "Chronological from oldest to newest" as if it followed from the evidence

options.text: Alphabetical by employer name
Reverse chronological from newest to oldest
Random order by relevance
options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "Random order by relevance" for the governing rule

questions.explanation: A German Lebenslauf runs reverse chronologically, newest first. The key is C, "Reverse chronological from newest to oldest". Option A ("Chronological from oldest to newest") is wrong: treats "Chronological from oldest to newest" as if it followed from the evidence. Option B ("Alphabetical by employer name") is wrong: confuses order with sorting. Option D ("Random order by relevance") is wrong: mistakes a surface feature of "Random order by relevance" for the governing rule.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The claim made in an Anschreiben
questions.learningObjective: Identify the claim in an Anschreiben

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: It demands a specific salary outright
It requests personal references only
It lists every grade from school
It states motivation and fit for the role

questions.explanation: An Anschreiben states motivation and fit for the role. The key is D, "It states motivation and fit for the role". Option A ("It demands a specific salary outright") is wrong: overstates the letter's demand. Option B ("It requests personal references only") is wrong: narrows the letter's purpose. Option C ("It lists every grade from school") is wrong: confuses cover letter with transcript.

questions.topic: Contract clause against administrative detail
questions.learningObjective: Spot the contract clause on admin detail

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: The clause that limits paperwork to essentials
The clause that adds more forms to fill
options.misconception: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes

options.text: The clause that sets a dress code
The clause that fixes working hours

questions.explanation: The clause that limits paperwork to essentials speaks against excessive admin detail. The key is A, "The clause that limits paperwork to essentials". Option B ("The clause that adds more forms to fill") is wrong: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes. Option C ("The clause that sets a dress code") is wrong: confuses admin with dress. Option D ("The clause that fixes working hours") is wrong: confuses admin with hours.
questions.hint: Look for a limit on paperwork.

Refuse to discuss salary at all

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: 'um' marks an exact hour
'in' marks a single point in time
'an' marks a specific day
'von ... bis' marks a span of time

questions.explanation: Bis' marks a span of time, while 'in', 'an', and 'um' mark point, day, or hour. The key is D, "'von ... bis' marks a span of time". Option A ("'um' marks an exact hour") is wrong: confuses hour with span. Option B ("'in' marks a single point in time") is wrong: confuses point with span. Option C ("'an' marks a specific day") is wrong: confuses day with span.
